heroText: Minsk is a spacious capital of Soviet avenues, parks and post-war architecture, with a calmer rhythm than many European capitals. Start on Independence Avenue, visit the National Library of Belarus for views, then walk Trinity Suburb beside the Svislach River. Minsk National Airport is well outside the city, so transfer planning matters.

areas.name: Upper Town
areas.text: Upper Town is the most atmospheric central base, close to churches, museums, the river and evening walks.

areas.name: Independence Avenue
areas.text: Independence Avenue suits business and sightseeing stays with metro access, large hotels and monumental architecture.

areas.name: Trinity Suburb
areas.text: Trinity Suburb is a small restored riverside quarter, good for quieter central stays near cafes and museums.

areas.name: Nemiga
areas.text: Nemiga is practical for shopping centres, nightlife and fast access between Upper Town and the river.

airports.name: Minsk National Airport (MSQ)
airports.text: Minsk National Airport is east of the city; transfers are long enough that taxis or planned buses should be checked before arrival.

airportTransfer.value: 40-60 min by taxi or airport bus to central Minsk
airportTransfer.distance: about 42 km east of the centre

stayOverview: Upper Town and Nemiga are best for a first central stay, Independence Avenue works for business and metro convenience, and Trinity Suburb gives a quieter riverside base close to museums and old-town walks.
hotelIntro: Minsk hotels are spread along broad central axes. Choose Upper Town for atmosphere, Independence Avenue for transport and larger hotels, Trinity Suburb for a slower riverside feel, or Nemiga for nightlife and shopping.
rentalCars: Use metro and taxis in Minsk; rent only for countryside trips or routes beyond the capital.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Stay near Upper Town or Nemiga if you want central walks without relying on taxis all day.

travelTips.title: Distances
travelTips.text: Minsk looks spacious on the map because avenues are wide; use the metro for longer cross-centre moves.

travelTips.title: Airport transfer
travelTips.text: Check current airport bus schedules before arrival, because Minsk National Airport is far from the centre.

travelTips.title: Day trip
travelTips.text: Mir Castle and Nesvizh Palace can be combined as a full heritage day trip from Minsk.

history.text: By 980, the area was incorporated into the early medieval Principality of Polotsk, one of the earliest East Slavic principalities of Kievan Rus'.
City authorities consider the date of 3 March 1067 to be the exact founding date of the city, though the town (by then fortified by wooden walls) had certainly existed for some time.
In 1129, the Principality of Minsk was annexed by Kiev, the dominant principality of Kievan Rus'; however in 1146 the Polotsk dynasty regained control of the principality.
In 1242, Minsk became a part of the expanding Grand Duchy of Lithuania.

history.label: 16th century
history.text: By the middle of the 16th century, Minsk was an important economic and cultural centre in the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.
In 1796, it became the centre of the Minsk Governorate.
A first public library was opened in 1836, and a fire brigade was put into operation in 1837.
In 1871, a railway link between Moscow and Warsaw ran via Minsk, and in 1873, a new railway from Romny in Ukraine to the Baltic Sea port of Libava (Liepāja) was also constructed.
A Workers' Soviet was established in Minsk in October 1917, drawing much of its support from disaffected soldiers and workers.
On 25 March 1918, Minsk was proclaimed the capital of the Belarusian People's Republic.
By 1924, there were 29 factories in operation; schools, museums, theatres and libraries were also established.
